questions.q: How does packaging change the deployment target compared to the direct-deploy pattern earlier chapters covered?
options: It doesn't change anything -- packages still deploy directly org by org
Packaging removes the need for a Dev Hub
Metadata gets bundled into a versioned, installable package, and that package version is what gets installed into an org, rather than metadata being deployed org-by-org
Packaging only works with Change Sets, never the CLI
questions.explain: Packaging shifts the pipeline's job to producing a trustworthy, versioned artifact that can be installed into any org, rather than deploying metadata directly into one specific org.

questions.q: What kind of org is required, authenticated via --target-dev-hub, to run sf package create and sf package version create?
options: Any Developer Edition org with no special configuration
A production org only
No org is required; these commands run entirely offline
A Dev Hub -- a special org enabled for package creation and scratch orgs
questions.explain: Both package commands require an authenticated Dev Hub, explicitly referenced since a CI runner has no implicit default org, just like other CLI commands in this course.

questions.q: What status does every newly created package version start with, regardless of who or what triggered its creation?
options: Released
Deprecated
Archived
Beta
questions.explain: A new package version is always marked beta at creation -- promotion to released status is a separate, deliberate action, never automatic.

questions.q: Why is it safe for a CI pipeline to automatically create a new beta package version on every pull request?
options: Because beta versions are automatically installed into production the moment they're created
Because beta versions bypass the 75% Apex coverage requirement entirely
Because beta versions can only be installed into scratch orgs and sandboxes for testing, so creating one automatically doesn't commit anyone to actually shipping it
Because creating a beta version is identical to promoting it to released
questions.explain: Beta versions are scoped to testing environments (scratch orgs, sandboxes) -- creating one automatically is a safe, reversible action distinct from the deliberate, separate promotion step.

questions.q: What coverage requirement must a package version's Apex code meet before it can be promoted to released status?
options: No coverage requirement applies to packages
50%, a lower bar than ordinary deployments
100%, a stricter bar than ordinary deployments
The same 75% minimum Apex code coverage requirement that gates any other production-bound Apex deployment
questions.explain: Package promotion is gated by the same platform-wide 75% Apex coverage minimum that applies to any production-bound Apex deployment.
